name: CachyOS
summary: Independent Linux distribution based on Arch Linux, designed to maximise responsiveness and execution speed through repositories recompiled for x86-64-v3/v4/Zen and advanced CPU process schedulers.
license: Open Source (GNU General Public License and various free licences from Arch Linux)

content.introduction: CachyOS is an independent Linux distribution based on **Arch Linux**, created in 2021 by an international team of developers and open-source contributors. The project aims to make full use of the power of modern microprocessors by improving the execution speed of binaries, the fluidity of desktop interactions and performance under heavy workloads (video gaming, software compilation, 3D modelling). While preserving the continuous update (rolling release) model and the vast software library of Arch Linux through Pacman and AUR, CachyOS stands apart through its custom build infrastructure and its advanced low-level settings.
content.what_is_it: Technically, CachyOS is a complete Linux system that enriches the Arch Linux foundation with a chain of specific hardware optimisations. Unlike the majority of general-purpose Linux distributions which compile their packages for the generic x86-64-v1 baseline in order to guarantee compatibility with old processors from 2003, CachyOS maintains its own software package repositories entirely recompiled with advanced processor optimisation flags and recent compilers (GCC and Clang/LLVM with LTO and PGO). The installer automatically detects the processor capabilities of the machine in order to configure the most optimised repositories.
content.cpu_architecture_levels_and_optimized_re: CachyOS offers software package repositories compiled for contemporary processor micro-architectures: **cachyos-v3** (for the x86-64-v3 architecture level, requiring AVX, AVX2, FMA, BMI1/BMI2, present on Intel Haswell / AMD Zen 1 and more recent processors); **cachyos-v4** (taking advantage of the AVX-512 vector instruction set on Intel Skylake-X/Ice Lake and AMD Zen 4/Zen 5 chips); and **cachyos-zen4** (specifically optimised for AMD Zen 4 and Zen 5 micro-architectures). These extended vector instructions significantly speed up multimedia libraries, mathematical computations and cryptography.
content.custom_linux_kernels_and_advanced_schedu: The technical core of CachyOS lies in its offer of heavily optimised Linux kernels (`linux-cachyos`), synchronised with the stable upstream versions and enriched with interactivity patches. CachyOS offers and supports a range of advanced CPU process schedulers: **BORE** (Burst-Oriented Response Enhancer, the default scheduler drastically improving interactive responsiveness under heavy computing load), **EEVDF** (optimised upstream), **BMQ / PDS** (from the Project C of Con Kolivas) and the **sched-ext** framework (extensible process schedulers in the kernel using eBPF). The dedicated graphical utility `cachyos-kernel-manager` makes it possible to test and switch between these different kernels in a few clicks.
content.storage_filesystem_btrfs_and_memory_tuni: By default, CachyOS installs its system on the modern **Btrfs** file system, configured with transparent block compression (zstd algorithm level 1) and an automated snapshot mechanism before each system update through Snapper or Btrfs Assistant. The system also supports ZFS (through precompiled kernel modules in the repositories), XFS and ext4. For RAM, CachyOS enables compressed swap in memory (**zram** with zstd) and the **ananicy-cpp** daemon, which dynamically readjusts process priorities in real time to guarantee priority to active windows, multimedia players and video games.
content.desktop_environments_and_dedicated_tooli: CachyOS is delivered with a user-friendly graphical installer based on Calamares (as well as a command-line TUI installer) and offers a wide range of preconfigured desktop environments (KDE Plasma by default, GNOME, XFCE, Hyprland, i3). The system includes exclusive in-house software tools: **Cachy-Browser** (hardened and optimised fork of Firefox compiled with LTO/PGO), `cachyos-package-installer`, `cachyos-bugreport` and the modern interactive shell **fish** configured by default. CachyOS is a fully open-source project governed by the GNU GPL free licences and the upstream licences of Arch Linux, with public development hosted on GitHub.
content.security_secure_boot_and_boot_chain_inte: The CachyOS wiki documents a verified boot procedure that remains optional and rests on keys created by the user. For GRUB, the command `grub-install --target=x86_64-efi --efi-directory=/boot/efi --bootloader-id=cachyos --modules="tpm" --disable-shim-lock` enables support for local authority keys, and the page points out that loading unnecessary modules in the boot manager presents a risk and that the command must be run only if Secure Boot is genuinely necessary. Enrolment goes through `sbctl`: `pacman -S sbctl`, then `sbctl create-keys`, then `sbctl enroll-keys --microsoft --firmware-builtin`. On ASUS and Gigabyte boards, the `--firmware-builtin` option can create duplicate `builtin-db` entries and cause a Secure Boot violation; the page then prescribes `sbctl enroll-keys --microsoft` alone, after deleting the keys in the firmware. `sbctl status` exposes the Installed, Owner GUID, Setup Mode, Secure Boot and Vendor Keys fields. With Limine from version 11.2.0, a BLAKE2B checksum of the configuration must be enrolled and each path in the configuration file must carry its fingerprint, failing which the manager stops on an explicit message and the configuration editor is disabled. For fwupd, the page has `fwupdx64.efi` signed by `sbctl` and sets `DisableShimForSecureBoot` in `/etc/fwupd/fwupd.conf`.
advantages: Leading-edge processor optimisations with dedicated repositories recompiled for x86-64-v3, v4 and Zen4.
Unique offer of optimised Linux kernels with advanced process schedulers (BORE, sched-ext, EEVDF).
Btrfs file system with zstd transparent compression and automated snapshots by default.
Optimised memory manager with zram swap in RAM and the ananicy-cpp adjustment daemon.
Excellent ease of use thanks to the Calamares installer and the in-house utilities (cachyos-kernel-manager).
Full access to the Arch Linux software library (Pacman and AUR) combined with a continuous rolling release model.
disadvantages: Rolling release model that may require periodic attention during major package updates.
Real performance gains depend heavily on the applications used and do not constitute a universal magic acceleration.
The x86-64-v3/v4 repositories require relatively recent microprocessors (incompatible with very old computers from before 2013).
Kernels with experimental schedulers (sched-ext) may require adjustments depending on the usage profile.
Less suited to critical production server environments requiring a software base frozen for ten years.
who_is_it_for: PC video game players (Linux gaming) looking for maximum responsiveness and kernels optimised for Proton/Wine.
Arch Linux users wishing to benefit from advanced hardware optimisations (AVX2, AVX-512) without compiling themselves.
Computing enthusiasts and testers curious to experiment with new CPU process schedulers (BORE, eBPF).
Content creators and developers using intensive computing workloads on modern multi-core processors.
who_is_it_not_for: System administrators looking for a distribution for critical servers with long-term commercial support.
Users owning very old personal computers with first-generation x86-64 processors (v1).
People preferring distributions with fixed and frozen stable versions (Debian Stable, Ubuntu LTS).
Absolute beginners in computing reluctant to accept the principles of the rolling release update model.
content.verdict: CachyOS is a Linux distribution oriented towards processor optimisation. By combining the Arch Linux base, repositories recompiled for the x86-64-v3/v4/Zen4 architectures, CPU schedulers (BORE, sched-ext) and Btrfs storage, it targets desktop and gaming uses.
content.origin_founders_and_publication_mileston:
The official About page names two founders, Peter Jung, known as ptr1337, and Vladislav Nepogodin, known as vnepogodin, both described as Founder and Developer, and it lists the roles of the wider team, among them a kernel maintainer who also contributes to the scx scheduler project. The page presents the distribution as a performance-focused rebuild of Arch Linux packages with a customised kernel.

The project blog provides the dated publication record. Its archive begins with an entry dated 2023-11-19 announcing the November 2023 update, followed by an entry dated 2023-12-01 on the x86-64-v4 repository made available for testing. Release announcements then continue with dated entries: 24 January 2026, 8 March 2026, 26 April 2026, 28 June 2026 and 9 August 2026, each titled as the release of that month, alongside entries from March, April, May, July, August and November 2025. On 2025-12-25 the project published a year-end review, CachyOS Recap 2025, reporting the members added to the team during the year, the sponsors and usage figures, and referring to the numbers of the previous year's recap.

Neither the About page nor the blog archive states a founding date or a first release date. The creation date of the source repositories is not used here as a founding date, and the earliest dated document found is the 2023-11-19 entry.

components.name: linux-cachyos
components.note: Project kernel presented on cachyos.org with BORE, sched-ext, BMQ and RT variants.

components.name: pacman
components.note: Package manager of the Arch Linux base, used with the x86-64-v3, x86-64-v4 and Zen4 repositories described on the project site.

components.name: Calamares
components.note: Graphical installer offered alongside a CLI installer, according to the project site and the installation guide.

components.name: sched-ext
components.note: Scheduler framework listed among the kernel features of the project.

relations.name: Arch Linux
relations.note: Rolling release Linux distribution on which CachyOS founds its package ecosystem and its tools.

relations.name: EndeavourOS
relations.note: Arch-based Linux distribution focused on a user-friendly installation and an experience close to the base.

relations.name: Nobara Linux
relations.note: Fedora-based Linux distribution oriented towards video gaming and performance optimisation.

relations.name: Bazzite
relations.note: Immutable operating system optimised for video gaming and handheld consoles.

variants.name: CachyOS Desktop Edition
variants.description: Desktop image described on the download page, with the online installer offering 17 or more desktop environments and window managers.

variants.name: CachyOS Handheld Edition
variants.description: Handheld image with preinstalled gaming tools, officially supporting ROG Ally, Steam Deck OLED and LCD, Legion Go and Legion Go S, with KDE Plasma as the only desktop.
